title: Priestly Duties and Inheritance
overview: Numbers Chapter 18 delineates the responsibilities, privileges, and provisions given to Aaron and the Levites concerning their sacred service in the tabernacle. God commands Aaron and his sons to bear the iniquity of the sanctuary and outlines the role of the Levites as ministers who assist but do not perform priestly functions. The chapter establishes the system of offerings and tithes as the means by which the priests and Levites are sustained, emphasizing the holiness required in their service and the divine provision for their inheritance. This chapter is pivotal in understanding the Levitical priesthood’s unique role in Israel’s worship and covenant relationship with God, highlighting themes of holiness, service, and divine provision.
structure:
**Verses 1-7: The Roles of Aaron and the Levites.** God instructs Aaron and his sons to bear the iniquity of the sanctuary and priesthood, while the Levites are assigned to assist in ministering but must avoid the sanctuary’s most holy areas to prevent death.

**Verses 8-19: The Priest’s Portion of Offerings.** God grants Aaron and his sons the heave offerings, wave offerings, firstfruits, and other holy things as their perpetual inheritance, emphasizing the sanctity and exclusivity of these gifts.

**Verses 20-24: The Inheritance of the Levites.** God declares that Aaron and his descendants will have no land inheritance among Israel, but the Levites will receive the tithes as their inheritance for their service in the tabernacle.

**Verses 25-32: The Heave Offering of the Levites’ Tithes.** Instructions are given for the Levites to offer a tenth of the tithes they receive as a heave offering to the Lord, which is then given to Aaron the priest, ensuring the continual support of the priestly family.

keyVerses.text: And the LORD said unto Aaron, Thou and thy sons and thy father's house with thee shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary: and thou and thy sons with thee shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood.
keyVerses.significance: This verse establishes the unique responsibility and accountability of Aaron and his descendants for the holiness and sin related to the sanctuary, underscoring the gravity of the priestly office.

keyVerses.text: And the LORD spake unto Aaron, Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither shalt thou have any part among them: I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel.
keyVerses.significance: God declares that the priests’ inheritance is not land but Himself, highlighting a spiritual inheritance that sets the priesthood apart from the tribal land allotments.

keyVerses.text: And, behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, even the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.
keyVerses.significance: This verse explains the provision for the Levites through the tithes of Israel, linking their inheritance directly to their sacred service in the tabernacle.

keyVerses.text: Thus speak unto the Levites, and say unto them, When ye take of the children of Israel the tithes which I have given you from them for your inheritance, then ye shall offer up an heave offering of it for the LORD, even a tenth part of the tithe.
keyVerses.significance: This instruction reveals the principle of sacred giving within sacred giving, showing the Levites’ duty to honor God by offering a portion of their own inheritance back to Him.

characters.name: Aaron
characters.description: The first high priest of Israel, chosen by God to bear the iniquity of the sanctuary and lead the priestly service. In this chapter, he and his sons receive specific instructions about their sacred duties and the offerings allocated to them.

characters.name: Levites
characters.description: Members of the tribe of Levi who assist the priests in ministering at the tabernacle. They are set apart to serve but are restricted from entering the most holy areas, and they receive tithes as their inheritance for their service.

characters.name: The LORD
characters.description: God speaks directly to Moses and Aaron, giving commands and establishing the priestly system. His instructions emphasize holiness, divine provision, and covenantal order.

themes.description: The chapter highlights the sacred responsibility of the priesthood to maintain holiness and bear the iniquity of the sanctuary, reflecting the broader biblical theme of God’s holiness requiring consecrated service.
God provides for the priests and Levites through offerings and tithes, illustrating His care for those who serve Him and the principle that spiritual service is supported by God’s provision.

Unlike other tribes, the priests and Levites receive no land inheritance but are given spiritual and material sustenance through offerings, emphasizing that their inheritance is tied to their service to God.

historicalContext: This chapter is set during the wilderness period of Israel’s journey from Egypt to the Promised Land, approximately the 15th century BC. The Levites were designated as a special tribe set apart for religious duties, distinct from the other tribes who received land allotments. The tabernacle served as the central place of worship and sacrifice, and strict regulations governed access and service to maintain holiness. The system of tithes and offerings was integral to sustaining the priestly class, reflecting ancient Near Eastern customs where religious functionaries were supported by the community’s offerings. Politically, Israel was a nomadic confederation under God’s direct guidance through Moses, with a theocratic structure emphasizing covenant obedience.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology sees this chapter as emphasizing the mediatorial role of Christ as the ultimate High Priest, with Aaron’s priesthood foreshadowing Christ’s perfect atonement and provision. The tithes and offerings point to God’s sovereign provision for His servants.

Dispensationalists interpret Numbers 18 as part of the Levitical priesthood’s earthly ministry, distinct from the New Testament priesthood of Christ. They emphasize the literal fulfillment of these laws in Israel’s history and the future restoration of the Levitical system in the millennial kingdom.

Early Church Fathers often allegorized the priestly duties as types of Christ’s intercession and the Church’s sanctification. They saw the Levites’ service and the offerings as symbols of spiritual cleansing and dedication to God.

crossReferences.connection: This passage explains how Christ’s priesthood surpasses Aaron’s, fulfilling and perfecting the priestly role described in Numbers 18.
Malachi’s call to bring tithes into the storehouse echoes the provision for the Levites and priests in Numbers 18.
This passage shows the seriousness of approaching the sanctuary improperly, paralleling the warnings in Numbers 18 about unauthorized access.
These verses also describe the Levites’ inheritance being the offerings of the people, reinforcing Numbers 18’s teaching.
Paul affirms that those who preach the gospel should live from the gospel, reflecting the principle of provision for ministers established in Numbers 18.

application: Recognize the seriousness of serving God with holiness and reverence, understanding the spiritual responsibility involved.
Trust in God’s provision for those who faithfully serve Him, whether in ministry or daily life.
Honor and support those who serve in spiritual leadership, remembering their God-ordained role and needs.
Offer your best to God as an act of worship, reflecting the principle of heave offerings and tithes.
Understand that your inheritance in Christ is spiritual and eternal, not merely earthly possessions.
Maintain purity in your approach to God, respecting His holiness and commands.
conclusion: Numbers 18 provides a vital foundation for understanding the sacred duties and divine provision for the priesthood and Levites. It underscores the holiness required in approaching God, the unique inheritance granted to those who serve Him, and the system of offerings that sustains their ministry. For believers today, it calls attention to the seriousness of spiritual service, the importance of honoring God’s appointed leaders, and the assurance that God faithfully provides for His servants. This chapter bridges the Old Testament priestly system with the greater fulfillment found in Christ, encouraging reverence, obedience, and generous worship.
timeline: c. 1446 BC - Wilderness Period during the Exodus

definitions.definition: A portion of an offering lifted up or presented to the Lord as a sacred gift, signifying dedication and consecration.
An offering ceremonially waved before the Lord, symbolizing the presentation and acceptance of the gift.
The responsibility borne by the priests for any sin or impurity associated with the sanctuary, requiring atonement.
One-tenth of produce or income given as an offering to God, supporting the Levites and priestly service.
The curtain separating the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place in the tabernacle, symbolizing the barrier between God’s holiness and man.
